title: Prompt-Stage Horizon Splitter — tenant-aware latency reservations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current admission and phase-splitting logic treats incoming requests as homogeneous 'phases' and schedules them primarily by token budgets and tenant weights. This leads to two issues in mixed workloads: (1) high-priority, short-horizon requests (e.g., short chats or embeddings) can be delayed behind long prefill requests that cause kernel warmups and KV cache churn; (2) kernel selection oscillation when interleaving many horizons (short vs long) yields suboptimal kernel reuse and higher tail latency.

Goal: Design and implement a Prompt-Stage Horizon Splitter (PSHS) that classifies requests by expected time horizon at admission and creates lightweight, tenant-aware reservations that guarantee time-bounded latency for short horizons while allowing longer-horizon requests to be scheduled opportunistically. The PSHS should integrate kernel-selection hints so that scheduling decisions prefer kernel-family affinity and reduce warmup frequency.

High-level design:
- Admission classifier: lightweight estimator at front of runtime that predicts expected horizon (short / medium / long) using request metadata (prompt length, decode settings, tenant profiles, recent token distributions). This estimator is conservative by default to avoid starvation.
- Horizon slots & soft reservations: maintain a small number of concurrent 'short-horizon slots' per tenant class and global opportunistic bucket for longer horizons. Short-horizon slots are soft reservations implemented as credit tokens that replenish at a tenant-configurable rate; unused credits can be borrowed by the opportunistic bucket under low load.
- Kernel affinity tagging: when admitting a request, annotate it with a preferred kernel family (e.g., large-batched fused-attn vs. small-batched kernel) based on horizon and sequence-length expectation. Scheduler uses this to prefer co-locating similar kernels on a device within the current window.
- Eviction and fallback: if a short-horizon reservation cannot be honored within its latency budget, the scheduler performs a fallback to a compatible, lower-cost model variant or a regional fallback endpoint. Eviction policy favors moving partial long-horizon work out of the way rather than preemptively dropping short-horizon requests.
- Fairness & tenant isolation: credits, while tenant-aware, are normalized by tenant tier and historical usage to avoid hard-locking capacity. A deficit counter prevents a tenant from consuming more than its share over a rolling window.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict hard reservations would guarantee latency but reduce cluster utilization; soft reservations aim for a middle-ground and are reversible under pressure.
- Conservative horizon estimation reduces misclassification but can underutilize short slots; we will iterate classifier thresholds with production telemetry.
- Kernel affinity may delay some high-throughput microbatches to preserve kernel locality; the policy will be parameterized and subject to A/B testing.

Success criteria / metrics:
- p99 tail latency for high-priority short-horizon requests improves by >= 35% under mixed workload benchmarks compared to baseline scheduler.
- Throughput degradation for long-horizon requests <= 8% under the same mixed workload.
- Kernel warmup events per hour reduced by >= 50% on benchmark hosts when using affinity hints.
- No regression in overall cluster utilization beyond acceptable threshold (<= 5% absolute drop).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for classifier, credit accounting, and kernel-affinity annotations.
- Deterministic scheduler simulator with synthetic tenant mixes (ratios: 70% long / 20% medium / 10% short; and mixed tier scenarios).
- Staging rollout: run PSHS on 10% of runtime nodes behind a feature flag; measure latency impacts and kernel-warmup rates.
- Canary rollout: route 5% of production traffic for 48h, compare against control via A/B metrics dashboard.

Implementation milestones:
1) Prototype admission classifier and token-based short-horizon credit pool (week 1-2).
2) Integrate kernel affinity tagging and scheduler hooks (week 3).
3) Simulator validation and bench runs with synthetic workloads (week 4).
4) Staging rollout + iterations (week 5).
5) Canary + roll forward to runtime-2.3 if targets met (week 6).

Dependencies and related work:
- Needs kernel selection telemetry hook from the kernel team (ENG-543219 referenced for kernel orchestration).
- Related fairness accounting logic: ENG-922338 tenant isolation work.
- Observability: requires new dashboard slices for horizon slot utilization and kernel-warmup events (console-ops ticket TBD).

Open questions:
- What is the right default horizon boundary (token count or token+decode-time estimate)? Proposed: short <= 64 tokens, medium 65-512, long > 512 — subject to tuning.
- How aggressively should credits replenish for bursty tenants? Start conservative (0.1 credits/sec) and tune from telemetry.
- Should kernel affinity be hard preference or soft? Start soft and expose knob in runtime config.

Rollout & mitigation plan:
- Feature flag + runtime config to disable PSHS per region.
- Canary with traffic weighting and automated rollback if p99 increases by >10% for high-priority tenants.
- Fallback variant routing in case of prolonged misclassification.

comments: 2026-02-18 — Proto: built basic estimator using prompt length + decode.max_tokens. Initial microbench: short-horizon p99 improved ~22% but long-horizon throughput dropped ~12% (too aggressive).

2026-02-25 — Design sync: agreed to switch to soft reservations and add deficit accounting; Marco to implement credit pool, Aisha to wire kernel-affinity tags. Action: add simulator scenarios with 3 tenant tiers.

2026-03-02 — Experiment: kernel-affinity labels reduced kernel warmups by ~48% on synthetic mixed workload (good). Observed misclassifications when system-wide queueing delayed admission; added admission TTL to re-evaluate horizon at scheduling time.

2026-03-07 — Code review: PR #512 in runtime repo added credit accounting and scheduler hook. Feedback: need clearer metrics emitted (horizon.slot_assigned, horizon.slot_evicted), and a circuit-breaker if cluster saturation exceeds 90%.
2026-03-09 — Staging plan approved. Next: enable PSHS on staging cluster behind feature flag and run 72h mixed load test. Monitoring alerts prepared for p95/p99 regressions and kernel-warmup spikes.
